taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_max_m.note: FEIS's incense-cedar review (Tollefson 2008, read 2026-10-15): "an evergreen tree that grows 66 to 187 feet (20-57 m) tall"; in presettlement giant sequoia forests "reportedly reached 225 feet (69 m) tall".

traits.leaf_length_m.note: FEIS's incense-cedar review (Tollefson 2008, read 2026-10-15): "Leaves are scale-like, 3 to 14 mm long, and form flat sprays".

traits.cone_length_m.note: Idžojtić, Dendrology (2019) p. 112, Calocedrus decurrens: seed cones 2-2.5(-3) cm long (FEIS, Tollefson 2008, gives 1.4-4 cm at maturity).

traits.sexual_system.note: Idžojtić, Dendrology (2019) p. 112, Calocedrus decurrens: monoecious.

traits.pollen_cone_length_m.note: FEIS's incense-cedar review (Tollefson 2008, read 2026-10-15): "Male cones are terminal on twigs and reach a length of 4 to 7 mm".

generator.params.note: Western redcedar's values, changed by hand for incense cedar: a dense, symmetrical, pyramid-shaped young crown with branches to the ground and flat sprays held more level (FEIS, Tollefson 2008). height_rate set so it reaches its reference height in a stand. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 19 m tall and 50 cm across at 60 years in a stand, set by hand; FEIS says trees grow slowly (Tollefson 2008). Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: By eye: cinnamon-brown, thick, fibrous and deeply furrowed bark (FEIS: "thick, fibrous, furrowed, and ridged"); bright green flat sprays; long narrow cones.

sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added with the core-species expansion (2026-10-15): sizes from FEIS and Dendrology, drawing values from western redcedar's.
